channel.title: Research Tape
channel.description: A daily AI-in-finance research tape: arXiv and SSRN, six items or fewer.

item.title: What LLM Trading Agents Actually Do in Production: A Six-Month, Population-Scale Record from Two Fleets
item.description: Risk settings determine LLM trading behavior more than written strategy text does.

item.title: TieOutBench: A Runnable, Rubric-Gated Evaluation Suite for Financial Analysis and Post-Trade Operations
item.description: Frontier financial LLMs fail to identify unreconciled baskets or mismatched confirmations.

item.title: What the Window Does Not Contain: Auditing Provenance in a Document-Grounded Instability Benchmark
item.description: Adding missing evidence to documents does not substantially reduce LLM answer instability.

item.title: Filtering without recursion and some of its uses in financial economics
item.description: Nonlinear filtering recovers volatility signatures from high-frequency data that linear methods cannot unbias.

item.title: GraphFAS: A Distributed System for Automated Graph Feature Generation and Selection in Industrial Transaction Networks
item.description: Non-parametric graph features enable fraud model interpretability that end-to-end GNNs cannot achieve.

item.title: The Market already Knew: A Pre-registered Falsification of TimesFM-3 on the SPY Implied-volatility Surface
item.description: Market-implied volatility forecasts outperform TimesFM-3 at both one and five-day prediction horizons.

item.title: Do Language Models Know Who Fails? Look-Ahead Bias in LLM Credit-Risk Assessment
item.description: LLM credit prediction beats baselines only because models memorized bankruptcy outcomes in training data.

item.title: When Financial Fine-tuning Fails: A Three-Level Detectability Analysis of Numerical Hallucination in Domain-Adapted Language Models
item.description: Financial domain fine-tuning increases LLM hallucination from 5% to 98% despite numeracy supervision.

item.title: Why Better Models Can Create Riskier Systems: Evidence from LLM Agents in Financial Markets
item.description: More capable LLM traders exhibit correlated behavior that concentrates rather than diversifies market risk.

item.title: Convex Modeling of Price Cross-Impact over Time
item.description: Models omitting cross-impact and transient decay systematically overestimate costs for relative-value trades.

item.title: Which Number Is Sticky? What Survives Source Withdrawal in Sequential LLM Financial Analysis
item.description: Controlling display of prior valuations matters more than disclosing their withdrawal in LLM financial analysis.

item.title: Correlated Beliefs, Correlated Trades: Agentic AI and Endogenous Volatility Amplification
item.description: Correlated AI beliefs amplify volatility through synchronized order flow, independent of individual forecast accuracy.

item.title: The Crisis of Entity Resolution in Heterogeneous AI Environments: Data, Financial, and Semantic Dimensions
item.description: Entity resolution errors cascade and compound across indexing, retrieval, and generation stages in AI systems.

item.title: The Analyst in the Prompt: Role, Retrieval, and Memory Biases in LLM Financial Analysis
item.description: LLM financial analysis bias stems mostly from interpreting the same evidence differently across roles, not from retrieving different evidence.

item.title: Testing semi-strong market efficiency in Brazilian football: A risk-adjusted machine learning approach
item.description: Machine learning models underperform Brazilian football betting odds.

item.title: Scaling Laws, Tabular Data and Actuarial Ratemaking Models
item.description: TabM scales with data substantially better than Transformers or MLPs on actuarial tasks.

item.title: RetailAgent: Structured Adverse Timing in Self-Conditioned Multimodal LLM Trading Agents
item.description: LLM agents exhibit predictable negative timing in sequential trading decisions.

item.title: Deep Hedging Under Realistic Market Frictions: A Regime-Conditional Empirical Study of Dynamic Option Hedging on Bitcoin Options
item.description: Deep hedging underperforms classical hedging methods on real options data with realistic transaction costs.

item.title: FORESIGHT-9: Prospective and Process-Aware Evaluation of Adaptive Trading Agents
item.description: A fixed equal-weight policy outperforms adaptive agents in 31 of 36 prospective runs.

item.title: FaVOR: LLM-Based Agentic Framework for Factor Mining via Empirical Validation
item.description: Automated factor mining optimized purely for returns breaks down across market regimes.

item.title: Ordinal Gates, Cardinal Bets: Matching LLM Confidence to the Financial Decision Operator
item.description: LLM confidence score portability requires joint optimization with the downstream operator.

item.title: Context Window Failures in Relational Foundation Models
item.description: Current relational foundation models cannot handle high-cardinality real-world data without pre-aggregation.

item.title: Trials-adjusted Out-of-Sample Gating for LLM-proposed Trading Strategies
item.description: No LLM-generated trading strategy survived out-of-sample validation with trials adjustment on real data.

item.title: Attributing Apparent AI Alpha: Factor Exposure, Leakage, Complexity, and Reasoning in Agentic Equity Research
item.description: Apparent AI alpha in equity selection is a benchmarking artifact, not skill.

item.title: AI Intermediation and Investor Information Processing: Evidence from Earnings Summaries on Social Media
item.description: AI summaries reduce retail investor opinion diversity but increase trading informativeness.

item.title: Agentic Empirical Asset Pricing: Methodological Foundations *
item.description: Agentic factor-discovery systems show inconsistent rankings across metrics and rolling re-executions.

item.title: AI Volatility Forecasts Under Stress: Performance, Tail Risk, and Ranking Reversals
item.description: Advanced volatility models deteriorate most during stress despite strong average-case performance metrics.

item.title: Canaries in the Gold Mine: Early Productivity Gains from Artificial Intelligence Creating Organization Capital
item.description: AI productivity emerges from building organization capital, not technology deployment alone.
